interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.name: Downtown Chattanooga
interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: derived from ramp_far_end=motorway: every exit-ramp chain merges onto another motorway, so nothing stops traffic at the far end. Free flow is inferred from read OSM link topology, not from a tag -- OSM does not tag the absence of a control. Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: derived from ramp_far_end=motorway: every exit-ramp chain merges onto another motorway, so nothing stops traffic at the far end. Free flow is inferred from read OSM link topology, not from a tag -- OSM does not tag the absence of a control. Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

stops.name: I-40 Weigh Station
stops.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ -- promoted to a weigh_station stop because 'Weigh Station' was the sole destination signed at this junction (a dedicated on-mainline scale ramp, not a shared exit with another place or road), at the sign's own milepost. Station and direction read 2026-10-07 from the Arkansas Highway Police weigh station list (Code of Arkansas Rules, permit rules appendix, https://codeofarrules.arkansas.gov/Rules/AppendixDocument?appendixID=226&partID=1006): this is Riverside, Interstate 40 westbound at mile 283, the first ramp west of the Hernando de Soto Bridge, with no eastbound side (eastbound I-40 is screened at Lehi, mile 274). It applies leaving Memphis only, so directions is forward, not both. Position re-read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 943052841, destination=Weigh Station, hgv=designated) leaves the westbound I-40 carriageway (way 943052840, ref I 40, drawn east to west) at highway=motorway_junction node 116871691 (35.1531424, -90.0829316); the weighbridges (ways 943052851 and 943052853) sit on the ramp, which merges back onto I-40 West at node 498743406. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 4 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 3.15. The old 2.4 sat on the Hernando de Soto Bridge.

stops.name: Lehi Weigh Station
stops.source: Station and direction from the Arkansas Highway Police weigh station list (Code of Arkansas Rules, permit rules appendix, https://codeofarrules.arkansas.gov/Rules/AppendixDocument?appendixID=226&partID=1006, read 2026-10-07): Lehi, Interstate 40 East, mile 274. Position read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 40945260, destination=Weigh Station) leaves the eastbound I-40 carriageway (way 40945256, ref I 40, drawn west to east) at highway=motorway_junction node 498744105 (35.1510263, -90.2555316), with the weighbridge (node 8261011620) and the scale area (way 340956254, 'Weigh Station (Truck) I-40') just east of it. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 89 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 13.43. Eastbound is this leg's reverse (Little Rock toward Memphis), so directions is reverse only; westbound I-40 is screened at Riverside, mile 283.

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ Position re-read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 943052841, destination=Weigh Station, hgv=designated) leaves the westbound I-40 carriageway (way 943052840, ref I 40, drawn east to west) at highway=motorway_junction node 116871691 (35.1531424, -90.0829316); the weighbridges (ways 943052851 and 943052853) sit on the ramp, which merges back onto I-40 West at node 498743406. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 4 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 3.15. The old 2.4 snap sat on the Hernando de Soto Bridge. The ramp_* fields were walked 2026-06-23 from the old snap and end at nodes 620883507 and 203622602 on the Memphis bank of the river; they were not re-walked here.

The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes and motorway_link destination tags, accessed 2026-06-23. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes projected onto the leg's route polyline (its archived geometry; OSRM only where none is archived), rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node on a motorway_link way at this exit, read from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ Highway read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap way refs (Overpass): this leg leaves Memphis on I-40 over the Hernando de Soto Bridge (way 1523781654, ref I 40), and the mainline stays ref I 40 alone until the I-55 junction at exit 279A west of here, where the I 40;I 55 concurrency begins. Position re-read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 943052841, destination=Weigh Station, hgv=designated) leaves the westbound I-40 carriageway (way 943052840, ref I 40, drawn east to west) at highway=motorway_junction node 116871691 (35.1531424, -90.0829316); the weighbridges (ways 943052851 and 943052853) sit on the ramp, which merges back onto I-40 West at node 498743406. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 4 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 3.15. The old 2.4 snap sat on the Hernando de Soto Bridge. The ramp_* fields were walked 2026-06-23 from the old snap and end at nodes 620883507 and 203622602 on the Memphis bank of the river; they were not re-walked here.
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

stops.name: I-40 Weigh Station
stops.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ -- promoted to a weigh_station stop because 'Weigh Station' was the sole destination signed at this junction (a dedicated on-mainline scale ramp, not a shared exit with another place or road), at the sign's own milepost. Station and direction read 2026-10-07 from the Arkansas Highway Police weigh station list (Code of Arkansas Rules, permit rules appendix, https://codeofarrules.arkansas.gov/Rules/AppendixDocument?appendixID=226&partID=1006): this is Riverside, Interstate 40 westbound at mile 283, the first ramp west of the Hernando de Soto Bridge, with no eastbound side (eastbound I-40 is screened at Lehi, mile 274). It applies leaving Memphis only, so directions is forward, not both. The same junction as the Memphis to Little Rock leg's I-40 Weigh Station, derived: this leg leaves Memphis on I-40 over the Hernando de Soto Bridge and its archived route geometry is identical to that leg's for the first seven miles (Tennessee-Arkansas line at 2.3 mi, this junction at 3.2 mi, exit 281 at 4.7 mi on both). Renamed from I-55 Weigh Station because the ramp is on I-40 before I-55 joins. Southbound I-55 is screened at Marion, mile 9, per the same list; that station is not on this leg yet. Position re-read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 943052841, destination=Weigh Station, hgv=designated) leaves the westbound I-40 carriageway (way 943052840, ref I 40, drawn east to west) at highway=motorway_junction node 116871691 (35.1531424, -90.0829316); the weighbridges (ways 943052851 and 943052853) sit on the ramp, which merges back onto I-40 West at node 498743406. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 4 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 3.15. The old 2.4 sat on the Hernando de Soto Bridge.

stops.name: Marion Weigh Station
stops.source: Station and direction from the Arkansas Highway Police weigh station list (Code of Arkansas Rules, permit rules appendix, https://codeofarrules.arkansas.gov/Rules/AppendixDocument?appendixID=226&partID=1006, read 2026-10-07): Marion, Interstate 55 South, mile 9. Position read 2026-10-07 from OpenStreetMap via the public Overpass API: the scale ramp (way 37921897, destination=Weigh Station) leaves the southbound I-55 carriageway (way 49565551, ref I 55;US 78, drawn north to south) at highway=motorway_junction node 445116050 (35.1950669, -90.2008509), with the weighbridge (node 8261049692) at the ramp's south end. at_mi derived: that node projected onto this leg's archived dense route geometry (world_data/us/geometry/tn.jsonl, 51 ft off the line), cumulative distance rescaled to leg miles, 11.29, a mile south of exit 10. Southbound is this leg's reverse (St. Louis toward Memphis), so directions is reverse only; northbound I-55 is screened at Bridgeport, mile 1, which this leg does not use (it joins I-55 from I-40 west of the river).
